name: Monport GT 50W Fiber
tagline: 50W Split fiber laser engraver with autofocus from Monport
tldr: Monport GT 50W Fiber is the 50W SKU on the Monport monport gt line. Monport GT 30W brings split-cabinet fiber marking with autofocus: useful for varying part heights. Verify optical power on the listing: do not assume combined-watt marketing.
mainObjective: Production-leaning fiber marking for small businesses

priceRange.note: Official Monport store, Oct 2026: $3,530 to $3,850 depending on bundle

engraveExample.description: Filled logo on stainless steel plate

pros: Largest field in the GT line: 200 × 200 mm, per Monport's spec table
1.25 mJ pulse energy, about 65% more than the entry GT
Same 0.10 mm listed marking depth as the GT 60W MOPA for about $1,100 less
cons: No colour marking: fixed 100–140 ns pulse from a Q-switched source
Beam quality listed at M² below 1.8, slightly looser than the entry GT's below 1.5
Pre-order and in-stock prices differ ($3,529.99 vs $3,599.99 in October 2026): check shipping dates

faq.question: What does the GT 50W add over the GT 30W?
faq.answer: Pulse energy and field size. Monport lists 1.25 mJ per pulse (0.75 mJ on the GT 30W), a wider 20–80 kHz frequency range, a 200 × 200 mm engraving area and a maximum marking depth of 0.10 mm. In our benchmark, a filled 10 × 10 cm logo on stainless takes about 3–8 minutes, against 4–11 on the 30W.

faq.question: Can the GT 50W cut thin sheet metal?
faq.answer: Monport claims cuts on thin metals under 3 mm for the GT series but publishes no per-model chart. The extra pulse energy makes multi-pass cut-outs in thin brass, stainless or aluminum quicker than on the 30W; expect many passes as you approach the top of that range, and use a dedicated fiber cutter for regular sheet work.

faq.question: GT 50W or GT 60W MOPA?
faq.answer: The GT 50W costs $3,529.99–3,599.99 on Monport's store (October 2026), about $1,100 less than the GT 60W MOPA at $4,699.99. Both list 0.10 mm marking depth. Pay for the MOPA only if you need colour on stainless or finer pulse control for plastics and anodized aluminum; for black marking and depth, the 50W is the better value.

standoutFeatures.title: 200 × 200 mm field
standoutFeatures.body: Monport fits the GT 50W with the largest lens of the GT range. More parts per batch on a fixture plate, or larger plaques in one pass without stitching.

standoutFeatures.title: More energy per pulse
standoutFeatures.body: 1.25 mJ per pulse against 0.75 mJ on the GT 30W, with a 20–80 kHz frequency range. Deeper logos and multi-pass cut-outs finish faster, at the same 10,000 mm/s top speed.

beginnerNotes: This profile is the 50W SKU on Monport GT Fiber. Read the TL;DR and benchmarks above, then compare other power options via the chips before buying.
proTips: Batch similar jobs to reduce setup. Use rotary only when quotes include cylinder work: it slows flat-stock days.
primaryUse: Mid-power fiber for shops marking metal daily

images.alt: Monport GT 50W Fiber laser engraver: Monport

editorialDepth.advantages: Monport GT Fiber 50W fits shops that mark stainless, aluminum, and tools daily without a CO₂ bay. A solid bench option for jewelry, tags, and small batches.
editorialDepth.limitations: Skip if wood, leather, or cast acrylic pay your bills. Deep metal cutting and large industrial panels often need more fiber headroom (60W or 100W) or a different machine class.
